messages:
Anika Patel: Quick check — I'm seeing a short-lived spike in client timeouts and 4xx on v1-generate for workloads that do heavy prefix caching. Anyone else seeing this?
Tom Nguyen: I noticed a few 504s too, looks correlated with long KV cache lookups. rough pattern: size of prefix cache keys went up -> tail latency climbed.
Sasha Li: Can you drop a dashboard link and a sample trace?
Anika Patel: Yep — dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/longtail/v1-generate-latency?orgId=1 look at the 95/99 lines and the per-route breakdown. Sample trace id: trace:abcd-2026-03-17-01 for a 504.
Matt R: Paging @oncall-bot for visibility, but seems like a request hot-keying issue. Might be batching + cache lock contention.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] Route v1-generate: 5xx spike detected (5-min avg > 3%) — alert id: A-7891
Anika Patel: Query I used in metrics: `sum(rate(http_server_exceptions_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (status)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))` — shows a 99th percentile jump.
Tom Nguyen: For traces, use the trace link in the dashboard or search by trace id in Tempo. Check spans around `kv_cache.lookup` and `batcher.wait`.
Sasha Li: Suggestion: temporarily lower the alert sensitivity for 4xx from 3%->5% while we confirm it's not client spam. Also reduce noise by excluding healthcheck paths.
Matt R: Agree on excluding healthchecks. Also propose a quick canary config: route a subset (10%) of traffic to a variant with `kv_cache.max_prefix_len=64` and `batcher.max_wait_ms=10` to see impact.
Anika Patel: I can spin that canary, but need links to the rollout UI. Which dashboards show prefix distribution?
Tom Nguyen: Prefix histogram is on the cache tab: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/cache/prefix-distribution. Use the `prefix_key_length` panel. Also look at `kv_cache_lock_seconds` for contention.
Sasha Li: For alert tuning, might be better to move to a composite alert: `rate(5xx) > X OR (rate(4xx) > Y AND 95p_latency > Z)`. Reduces false positives when latency normal.
Anika Patel: I'll try the canary config and post results. If anyone can grab a few sample traces (especially ones showing `kv_cache.miss -> batcher.wait` > 200ms) paste them here.
Tom Nguyen: grabbing traces now, will post a couple.
Matt R: If the canary looks good, we should update the autoscale policy for that pool — current burst policy is too conservative.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary for v1-generate variant `kv-prefix-tweak` at 1895012370 by Anika Patel. CI: passed.
Anika Patel: canary started at 1895012370, routing 10% traffic. Monitoring for 10m.
Tom Nguyen: First trace: trace:ef12-2026-03-17-02 shows `kv_cache.lookup` 180ms + `batcher.wait` 120ms -> total tail 420ms. Posting link: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/ef12-2026-03-17-02
Sasha Li: Thanks — seems like contention. If canary reduces 99p by >30% we roll it.
Anika Patel: 5m in — 99p down ~35%, 4xx back to baseline. Will keep running and then promote.
Matt R: Nice. After promotion let's open a follow-up to investigate cache eviction and prefix sharding.
Anika Patel: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Tom Nguyen: cc @sre-team for FYI on alert change suggestions.
Sasha Li: Filing an observability ticket to formalize the composite alert suggestion and add the prefix distribution panel to the main SRE dashboard.
Anika Patel: Closing the thread once canary fully promoted — will post final timestamps.
